welcome.intro: Welcome to your first step in mastering mathematics! In this lesson, you'll discover how numbers work and build a strong foundation for all your future math learning.

topic1.title: Understanding Numbers
topic1.desc: Learn what numbers are and how we use them every day

topic2.title: Place Value System
topic2.desc: Discover how position gives meaning to digits

topic3.title: Comparing & Patterns
topic3.desc: Master comparing numbers and spotting patterns

numberLine.title: Interactive Number Line
numberLine.instruction: Numbers follow a pattern from 1 to 10. Each number is one more than the previous!

number.definition: A number is a mathematical object used to count, measure, and label. Numbers help us understand quantities and order.

counting.title: Counting from 1 to 100
counting.description: Numbers follow a pattern. After 9, we use two digits. The first digit shows how many "tens" and the second shows how many "ones".

exercise.question: What number comes after 19?
exercise.hint: Think about counting: seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, ...

placeValue.definition: Place value tells us what each digit in a number represents based on its position.

example.problem: What is the value of the digit 7 in the number 572?

step1.title: Identify the position of 7
step1.content: In 572, the digit 7 is in the tens place

example.hint: Look at which position the 7 is in: ones, tens, or hundreds?

exercise.question: In the number 286, what is the value of the digit 2?
exercise.hint: The digit 2 is in the hundreds place. What is 2 × 100?
exercise.solution1: The digit 2 is in the hundreds place.

comparing.description: We use symbols to compare numbers:
comparing.tip: Think of the symbols as hungry mouths that always want to eat the bigger number!

exercise.question: Which symbol makes this true: 45 ___ 54?
exercise.explanation: 45 < 54 because 45 is less than 54. The symbol points to the smaller number (45).
exercise.hint: Which number is smaller? The symbol should point to it.

even.label: Even Numbers
even.definition: Can be divided by 2 with no remainder

exercise1.question: Which of these numbers is odd?
exercise1.explanation: 47 is odd because it ends in 7. Odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9.
exercise1.hint: Look at the last digit of each number.

exercise2.question: What is the smallest three-digit even number?
exercise2.hint: Think about the smallest three-digit number, and check if it's even.

conclusion.title: Congratulations!
conclusion.message: You've mastered the fundamentals of number sense! These skills are the building blocks for all mathematics.
